title: C++: RAII - destructors run at the closing brace

steps.note: Inside the inner `{ }` block, `b` is constructed too.
`std::make_unique` creates a Resource on the **heap**, owned by the smart pointer `c` (which itself lives on the stack).
steps.out:
open A
open B
open C

steps.note: At `}` every object of the block is destroyed **in reverse order of construction**: `c`'s destructor deletes the heap Resource ('close C'), then `b` ('close B'). No `delete` anywhere. This is **RAII**: *Resource Acquisition Is Initialisation*.
steps.out:
open A
open B
open C
close C
close B

steps.note: When main ends, `a` is destroyed. The order is **deterministic**, so you know exactly when files close and locks release.
steps.out:
open A
open B
open C
close C
close B
end of main
close A
